videos.review: Group file labels this 'emily', but it is the client's view of remote Corvo. On the Edge of the World pier he walks in with the sword, goes neutral while the wheel is open (~3.7 s) and draws the pistol (~4.7 s). He reloads with the pistol raised and casing sparks (5.6-8.4 s), then holds a steady aim (9.4-14 s). Limbs are intact and his feet stay planted.

Over two rounds he stands with his arm extended and aims, with fire recoil and a reload arm-bend (~2.2 s, ~4.5 s). He turns side-on to holster (~11 s), idles neutral, re-equips pistol and sword (~14.4 s) and aims again. The body yaw swings about 90 degrees between the aim stance and the neutral idle, which is a minor polish issue.

Group file labels this 'corvo', but it is the host's view of remote Emily. The sequence matches Corvo's: sword, neutral during the wheel, pistol draw (~4.7 s), raised-pistol reload with sparks (5.6-8.4 s), then a steady aim. Pose is clean and her feet are planted.
Over two rounds she aims with an extended arm, with fire and reload. She holsters side-on (~11-13.5 s), re-equips and aims (~14.6 s), then sheathes. Transitions are smooth and nothing breaks.

summary: Both partners read the pistol draw, aim, fire and reload, and the holster and re-equip, cleanly, with the native prop in hand; the aim-stance yaw offset is only a polish issue.

videos.review: He aims with his arm extended, holding a distinct native crossbow prop (limbs visible in a zoomed crop, different from the pistol). Fire recoil kicks the arm up (~2.0 s, ~4.8 s), followed by a reload arm-bend. He holsters side-on (~11-13.5 s), re-equips and aims again. The stance is the same generic one-arm ranged pose as the pistol.
Same two-round aim, fire, reload, holster and re-equip cycle as v29. The pose is stable, his feet stay planted and the transitions are clean.
Emily runs the same cycle: arm extended with the crossbow, recoil and reload (~2.2 s, ~4.5 s), side-on holster (~11-13.5 s), re-equip and aim, then sheathe at ~16.9 s. Clean.
Same cycle as v29 with no defects.

summary: The crossbow aim, fire, reload and holster read correctly for both partners with the crossbow prop in hand; the stance reuses the generic one-arm ranged pose.

videos.review: Dark scene, back view, judged from brightened crops. The cook pose reads (sword raised, grenade hand forward, 1.0-2.3 s), but at release (~2.40-2.47 s) the body snaps about 0.5-0.75 m sideways in two frames and drifts back over ~0.5 s. After the source's own grenade blast (~4.5 s) the partner slides toward the camera and then holds the arms-out armed idle, static, to the end.
The cook and low throw read correctly: sword raised, throw with a follow-through turn (~2.3-2.8 s) and no obvious pop. Afterwards he shows the same post-blast slide and static armed idle.

The cook pose and throw read, but at release her whole body jumps about 0.35 m sideways in a single frame (2.40 to 2.43 s) and eases back by ~2.9 s. After the blast she shows the same slide and static armed idle.
The cook (sword raised, grenade hand forward) and low throw with a body turn read naturally, with no pop at release. Afterwards she shows the same post-blast slide and static armed idle.

summary: The cook and throw are recognizable for both partners, but on the high throw the body pops sideways at release (Corvo about 0.5-0.75 m over two frames, Emily about 0.35 m in one frame); the low throws are acceptable.

He recovers, holsters to a neutral idle (14.7-18.9 s) and re-arms. His hand stops short of the floor during placement, a minor issue.
